title: XM-Sparse: High-Throughput Sparse-Attention LLM Serving over Scale-up Memory Pools
summary: XM-Sparse replaces PCIe-based host-memory KV offloading by aggressively offloading both the sparse KV cache and the indexer K-index cache to a scale-up memory pool, using TMA-fused tile-level retrieval for dynamic KV and GPU-initiated DMA prefetching for predictable index pages. It costs implementation complexity atop SGLang, access to scale-up memory expansion hardware, and the engineering burden of coordinating prefetch with latency-critical decode operations. It can fail if real (non-emulated) memory-pool bandwidth or latency diverges from the emulation, if access-pattern assumptions break for other models or workloads, or if hot KV buffers still bound HBM concurrency at extreme context lengths.
rationale: The technique depends on emerging scale-up memory pool hardware (X-Mem) unavailable on a single 24 GB GPU or via third-party APIs, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable now.
technique: Sparse-attention KV offloading over scale-up memory pools

claims.statement: XM-Sparse replaces PCIe-based host-memory KV offloading by aggressively offloading both the sparse KV cache and the indexer K-index cache to a scale-up memory pool, using TMA-fused tile-level retrieval for dynamic KV and GPU-initiated DMA prefetching for predictable index pages. It costs implementation complexity atop SGLang, access to scale-up memory expansion hardware, and the engineering burden of coordinating prefetch with latency-critical decode operations. It can fail if real (non-emulated) memory-pool bandwidth or latency diverges from the emulation, if access-pattern assumptions break for other models or workloads, or if hot KV buffers still bound HBM concurrency at extreme context lengths.

Up to 4.98x higher decode throughput than PCIe-based ECHO (and 4.52x over HiSparse, 1.34x over naive same-platform integration) across 16K-1M contexts on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.3 with an emulated scale-up memory pool.
